candidates.rationale: The metadata resolves this alias-surfaced API to generic Result::is_err_and. Its source exposes no relation to LockResult's classified lock-poisoning state; a matching declaration would instead specify the canonical Result method globally.
The owner is core::result::Result, whose is_ok discriminant contract already exists in vstd. An alias-specific declaration would duplicate that specification without modeling lock-poisoning state.

The supplied signature belongs to generic Result::is_ok_and, not a LockResult-specific implementation. The source provides no public relation to the classified lock runtime state, so an alias-scoped trusted contract would be misleading.

The source and owner describe generic Result::iter. IteratorSpec can characterize that canonical iterator, but no distinct contract at the LockResult alias surface can relate it to hidden lock-poisoning state.

The returned Result::IterMut yields mutable references whose eventual writes require a prophetic relation to final(self), which current IteratorSpec vocabulary does not provide; the alias also exposes no lock-state model.

The metadata resolves to generic Result::map, whose closure-aware contract already exists in vstd. Re-specifying it through LockResult would duplicate the canonical contract and would not characterize hidden lock state.
